speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your infant's recurrent stridor and wheezing, could you please describe the specific activities that trigger these episodes and how long they typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia with associated gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). The combination of stridor and wheezing worsened by feeding, crying, and neck flexion, along with post-prandial vomiting, is highly characteristic of this condition in an infant.
